architecture.summary: A small Spring-style service with controller-service-repository layering, a KYC HTTP integration, a risk-scoring service, JPA repository persistence, Kafka event publishing and contract/example documentation.

modules.name: API layer
modules.responsibility: Expose onboarding and status REST endpoints.

modules.name: Application service
modules.responsibility: Orchestrate duplicate check, KYC, risk scoring, status decision, persistence and event publishing.

modules.name: Domain model
modules.responsibility: Represent Customer state and state transitions.

modules.name: Integrations
modules.responsibility: Call KYC provider and publish Kafka events.

runtime.name: Spring application
runtime.description: Application name and integration settings are configured in application.yml.

target_architecture.summary: Keep the current modular service shape, but move volatile business decisions and integration configuration into explicit policies/configured clients before considering a broader platform or service split.

tech_stack_options.name: Hardened Spring Boot modular service
tech_stack_options.fit: Best fit for the compact repository because REST, validation and JPA dependencies are already Spring-based.
tradeoffs: Does not independently scale KYC/risk/eventing components

tech_stack_options.name: Split KYC/risk/eventing services
tech_stack_options.fit: Potential future option only if independent scaling or ownership boundaries emerge; current evidence does not justify the added operational complexity.
tradeoffs: Requires stronger contract and event governance

migration_steps.description: Inject the configured risk threshold and add boundary tests for scores 70 and 71.
Inject and configure the KYC HTTP client with timeout/retry policy.
Add CI contract validation for OpenAPI/WSDL examples before larger technology migration work.

open_questions: Whether KYC, risk scoring or event publishing need separate runtime ownership is not proven by this compact repository.

observations.title: Business decision sits in application service
observations.description: The ACTIVE vs MANUAL_REVIEW decision is implemented in OnboardingService rather than a dedicated policy object.

architecture.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  Client[API Client] --> Controller[OnboardingController]
  Controller --> Service[OnboardingService]
  Service --> Repo[CustomerRepository]
  Service --> KYC[KycClient]
  Service --> Risk[RiskScoringService]
  Service --> Kafka[OnboardingEventPublisher]
  Repo --> DB[(Customer DB)]
  KYC --> ExternalKYC[External KYC Provider]
  Kafka --> Topic[(customer.onboarding.started)]

findings.title: KYC client creates RestTemplate internally
findings.description: The KYC client constructs RestTemplate directly, which makes configuration and testing less explicit.
findings.recommendation: Inject an HTTP client bean with timeout and retry policy.

refactoring.title: Extract onboarding decision policy
refactoring.description: Move the ACTIVE/MANUAL_REVIEW decision and threshold into a dedicated policy object or configuration-driven service.
refactoring.benefit: Business logic becomes easier to test and change.
prerequisites: Add tests for risk score boundary values

refactoring.title: Inject KYC HTTP client
refactoring.description: Inject RestTemplate or a typed client instead of constructing it inside KycClient.
refactoring.benefit: Improves testability and makes timeouts/retries configurable.

modernization.title: Add contract validation to CI
modernization.description: Use the OpenAPI/WSDL contracts and examples as executable contract checks.
modernization.target_state: CI validates DTOs, examples and REST/SOAP contracts for drift.
modernization.benefit: Prevents documentation and implementation from diverging.
